findings.reason: either §3 must declare the ranked section rows it requires (and §2's "Nothing else is added" must yield to it) or both done-whens must be restated at plan granularity, and one of the two nodes would otherwise report green on a measure it never met.
findings.text: §3 measures "the ranked order puts the section with the largest downstream reach first" and writes its placing signal into "the existing `reason` field of `immediate_roadmap` rows … one vocabulary for plan rows and section rows alike", but at the base revision the `immediate_roadmap` rows are plan rows built from the `ready` list (`reckon/roadmap.py:3542-3560`), and the only per-section rows are `row["section_readiness"]` entries of `{section, ready, blockers}` (`reckon/roadmap.py:3378-3394`) with no `reason` field and no rank; §2, the section §3 cites as the source of section awareness, closes with "Nothing else is added" beyond a `sections` list on `critical_path`/`open_paths` and the existing `unlocks`, so no section in the plan declares who produces a ranked section list — which §7:111 also consumes ("the ten highest-ranked ready sections with their `reason`", "the three ready sections with the largest reach") — leaving the implementing node either to invent a surface no section declares or to write a measure it cannot satisfy

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every code anchor cited by the in-scope sections resolves at the line named or near it (table above), including `reckon roadmap --brief`'s host command and the dropped-`external-data`/`flat-priority-signal` references.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every in-scope section names a control that must fail on the unfixed code (s2/s3/s4 base commit, s5 the declared-edge fixture emitting nothing, s7 the base plus a changed-edge arm), and s7 states the parity test is a drift guard rather than the control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs and the per-mount counts land on the plan's cumulative record `docs/evidence/archive/a-project-reads-as-one-picture-landed.html`, which exists and resolves; no in-scope section writes evidence to a scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols the in-scope sections introduce (`undeclared-wait`, `overlapping-scope`, `run-blocked`, `held-path`, `project_brief`) describe the mechanism; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches them, and the two "first planned … is dropped" sentences are decisions in plan prose, not code comments.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3's done-when ranks a section first and §7's brief lists the ten highest-ranked ready sections, but the mechanism §3 states extends `priority` over `immediate_roadmap` plan rows and writes into a `reason` key that section rows do not have.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 lifts section edges and exposes them, §3 reweights the ranking, §4 seats runs on their section, §5 emits two wiring findings, §7 composes one brief; each closes on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the changed map at line 25 gives s3:[s2], s5:[s2,s4], s7:[s2,s3,s4,s5] and s8:[s2,s3,s4,s5,s7], each matching what the section's own text reads: §5 consumes §4's run classification and §2's edges, and §7 composes from §2 to §5 as it states.
